questions.q: Which two emotions does the summary say dominate most people's money decisions?
a: Fear and greed
Hope and pride
Shame and envy
Trust and generosity
questions.why: The overview says fear keeps us from investing while greed pushes us to spend, and both keep us in the rat race.

questions.q: What does the summary call anything that takes money out of your pocket each month?
a: A liability
An asset
A royalty
An investment
questions.why: The summary defines liabilities as things like car payments, mortgages and debt that drain money every month.

questions.q: What does the summary advise doing with the extra money from a raise?
a: Investing it in something that builds wealth
Spending it on an improved lifestyle
Saving it in a low-interest bank account
Using it to buy a bigger house
questions.why: The overview warns that upgrading your lifestyle eats the raise, while investing it can build wealth.

questions.q: What does paying yourself first mean in the summary?
a: Investing your chosen portion before paying bills
Buying yourself a gift at the start of each month
Clearing every debt before you spend anything
Taking your salary before your employees do
questions.why: The summary says to invest the money you want for stocks or financial education first, then pay bills, which creates useful pressure.

questions.q: How does the summary distinguish your job from your business?
a: Your job pays the bills while your business builds wealth
Your job should be quit as soon as possible
Your business should replace your job within a year
Your business should stay small and unprofitable
questions.why: The summary advises keeping your job, minding your own business, and building assets on the side until they become your main income.
